subject.title: [Bug]: Memory Multimodal Indexing - Gemini API rejects OGG/Opus audio files

question: Should Gemini multimodal memory keep advertising OGG/Opus by adding an owned transcode path, or should OpenClaw narrow Gemini audio support to MP3/WAV with clear diagnostics and docs?
rationale: Both fixes are plausible, but one removes advertised formats while the other adds media conversion dependency and validation scope, so automation should not choose the product boundary alone.

options.title: Narrow Gemini audio support
options.body: Document and enforce MP3/WAV for Gemini multimodal memory, skipping or failing unsupported audio with clear diagnostics and no new transcode dependency.

options.title: Own a transcode path
options.body: Keep OGG/Opus advertised by converting unsupported audio to a Gemini-supported format before embedding, with dependency, size, failure, and live-provider proof.

options.title: Defer to broader multimodal design
options.body: Keep this open under the wider multimodal memory product decision if maintainers want one shared contract for all provider-specific format limits.

recommendation.title: Narrow Gemini audio support
recommendation.body: Document and enforce MP3/WAV for Gemini multimodal memory, skipping or failing unsupported audio with clear diagnostics and no new transcode dependency.

likelyOwner.reason: The shipped multimodal memory subset and docs/config boundary came from this PR history, making gumadeiras the closest routing candidate for the product choice.
